argument: One Weapon Maneuver breaks the flat damage budget. Shield Slam cites a 2 Armor prerequisite (Adept, 2 ranks) and its Weak/Standard/Strong lines print 1/2/3 at lines 377-381, but the card is a flat-damage maneuver, not a Basic Attack, so its base row must be the Novice row 2/4/6, with 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 already following at lines 383 and 385. The 1/2/3 value is the attribute-scaled Basic-card floor and only applies where a stated attribute is added; Shield Slam adds none, so 1/2/3 is off-budget. Broken value 1/2/3, expected 2/4/6. Every sibling flat maneuver confirms the row: Riposte, Cyclone, Brace and Renewal each open at 2/4/6, and Dual Strike totals 2/4/6, so Shield Slam is the lone outlier. Minimal fix: raise lines 377/379/381 to 2/4/6 damage. Separately, Weapon Focus escalates the booster to +2 and +3 damage tiers at lines 61 and 63; the convention sanctions only the single-step tier bump expressed as +1 damage tier, and a three-step bump on a Master row (21) leaves the budget table, so those two lines exceed the allowed booster and should be restated as single-step bumps. Cost, gate and Discipline-count math are otherwise sound: costs sit at 2/4/8 with the Level 3 and Level 7 gates, and no card requires more than 3 ranks, so the max-3 ladder holds.

evidence.claim: Shield Slam prints 1/2/3 as flat maneuver damage; as a 2-Armor flat card it should sit on the Novice row 2/4/6, so all three lines are one step low.
Riposte, the neighboring 2-rank Blades maneuver, keys its base damage to 2/4/6 then 6/9/12 and 9/15/21, showing the row Shield Slam should match.
Cyclone also opens at 2/4/6 for a 3-rank card, confirming the Novice base row is the norm for flat maneuvers.

evidence.claim: Weapon Focus scales to two and then three damage tiers, exceeding the single sanctioned tier bump; the Adept and Master lines need single-step phrasing.
Recomputed every flat row in the chapter: 2/4/6, 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 all hold except Shield Slam's base 1/2/3, and no card exceeds 3 required ranks.
